item.title: Sinner brushes past Shelton, sets Djokovic Australian Open SF
item.description: Jannik Sinner kept his Australian Open three-peat bid rolling on Wednesday, when he produced another ruthless performance to brush aside Ben Shelton and extend his stranglehold against the American. The two-time defending champion, unbeaten in Melbourne since 2023, never looked in serious danger against Shelton, moving past the eighth seed 6-3, 6-4, 6-4 to book his place in the semi-finals. item.title: Two sets up, no way through: Musetti joins rare major retirement list
item.description: When Lorenzo Musetti walked to the net on Tuesday night at the Australian Open, the scoreboard told a story that tennis almost never sees. Two sets to love up against Novak Djokovic, the Italian was forced to retire in their quarter-final, joining one of the sport’s most painful and unusual footnotes: players who have led by two sets at a Grand Slam and never finished the match. item.description: Ben Shelton may have been stopped at a major for the fourth time by Jannik Sinner, but the American left Rod Laver Arena on Wednesday with plenty to be encouraged by after another deep Grand Slam run. item.title: Harrison & Skupski power into Australian Open doubles final
item.description: Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski extended the impressive early run of their new partnership on Thursday afternoon at the Australian Open, where they secured a place in the men’s doubles final. item.title: Old King, New Order: Djokovic & Sinner set for Australian Open SF blockbuster
item.description: There are nights at Melbourne Park when the future knocks loudly on the door, and others when history refuses to move aside. item.description: Novak Djokovic is widely regarded as one of the best returners in tennis history. item.title: Gadecki/Peers go back to back at home, successfully defend Australian Open mixed doubles title
item.description: Olivia Gadecki and John Peers kept their cool to forge a repeat triumph on home soil Friday at the Australian Open.
